abstract: |
  *Objective.* To determine whether corroboration across national physician data sources is associated with confirmation that an otolaryngologist remains in practice at the indexed location.

  *Study Design.* Stratified mystery-caller telephone audit.

  *Setting.* National sample of U.S. otolaryngology practices, May to July 2026.

  *Methods.* Otolaryngology listings in the National Plan and Provider Enumeration System (NPPES) were linked by National Provider Identifier to active board-certification records and the ENTHealth physician directory. Trained callers contacted stratified samples and recorded whether the named physician remained at the contacted practice or continued to practice otolaryngology elsewhere. Supplemental calls to physicians identified only in NPPES are ongoing.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo    = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  fig.dpi = 300
)

library(here)
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(forcats)
library(survey)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)
library(scales)

# ── Load call log ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
f_all <- tail(sort(list.files(here("data", "processed"),
                               pattern = "ent_phase2_all", full.names = TRUE)), 1)
calls <- read_csv(f_all, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  mutate(npi = as.character(npi))

# ── Load Euler zone demographics ───────────────────────────────────────────────
# The Euler zone file was produced by the ~/isochrones/ project. It contains
# one row per NPI with registry-overlap zone assignment and physician demographics.
euler <- read_csv(
  path.expand("~/isochrones/publication_materials/figures/ent_data_integrity/ent_euler_zone_npi_assignments_with_demographics.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
) |> rename(npi = npi_chr) |> mutate(npi = as.character(npi))

# ── Euler zone population counts ───────────────────────────────────────────────
pop_counts <- euler |> count(zone) |> tibble::deframe()
N_nppes_total      <- sum(c(pop_counts["1_nppes_only"], pop_counts["2_nppes_board"],
                             pop_counts["3_nppes_ent"],  pop_counts["8_triple_match"]),
                          na.rm = TRUE)
N_aboto            <- sum(c(pop_counts["2_nppes_board"], pop_counts["8_triple_match"]), na.rm = TRUE)
N_enthealth        <- sum(c(pop_counts["3_nppes_ent"],   pop_counts["8_triple_match"],
                             pop_counts["6_ent_only_with_npi"], pop_counts["7_ent_only_no_npi"]),
                          na.rm = TRUE)
N_triple           <- pop_counts["8_triple_match"]
N_nppes_board      <- pop_counts["2_nppes_board"]
N_nppes_ent        <- pop_counts["3_nppes_ent"]
N_nppes_only       <- pop_counts["1_nppes_only"]
N_euler_total      <- nrow(euler)   # all 7 overlap zones combined

# ── Normalise datasets column → overlap_zone ──────────────────────────────────
# Two REDCap data-entry spellings both refer to the NPPES+ABOto stratum.
calls <- calls |>
  mutate(
    overlap_zone = case_when(
      datasets %in% c("ABO, NPI but not ENT Health",
                      "ABO, NPI but no ENTHealth")   ~ "NPPES+ABOto",
      datasets == "ABO, NPI, ENT Health"              ~ "NPPES+ABOto+ENTHealth",
      TRUE                                            ~ NA_character_
    )
  )

# ── Join Euler demographics ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
df <- calls |>
  left_join(
    euler |> select(npi, zone, credential_class, billed_any_part_b,
                    years_since_enum, bog_region),
    by = "npi"
  )

# ── Derive validity outcomes ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
# taking_new_patients mapping:
#   "Yes"                          → at location (confirmed_yes); active (confirmed_yes)
#   "No-practice is full..."       → at location (confirmed_yes); active (confirmed_yes)
#   "No-on leave of absence..."    → at location (confirmed_yes); active (confirmed_yes)
#   "No-changed practices"         → NOT at location (confirmed_no); STILL active (confirmed_yes)
#   "No-retired or no longer..."   → NOT at location (unknown); NOT active (confirmed_no)
#   All other / NA                 → unknown

df <- df |>
  mutate(
    physician_at_location = case_when(
      taking_new_patients %in% c(
        "Yes",
        "No-practice is full but physician does still see established patients",
        "No-on leave of absence (like parental leave)"
      )                                                              ~ "confirmed_yes",
      taking_new_patients == "No-changed practices"                  ~ "confirmed_no",
      TRUE                                                           ~ "unknown"
    ),
    physician_active = case_when(
      taking_new_patients %in% c(
        "Yes",
        "No-practice is full but physician does still see established patients",
        "No-on leave of absence (like parental leave)",
        "No-changed practices"
      )                                                              ~ "confirmed_yes",
      taking_new_patients == "No-retired or no longer practicing medicine" ~ "confirmed_no",
      TRUE                                                           ~ "unknown"
    ),
    invalid_reason = case_when(
      phone_validity_flag == "invalid_format"                        ~ "wrong_disconnected_number",
      taking_new_patients == "No-changed practices"                  ~ "relocated",
      taking_new_patients == "No-retired or no longer practicing medicine" ~ "retired_inactive",
      office_answered == FALSE & phone_validity_flag == "valid"      ~ "not_reached_valid_phone",
      taking_new_patients == "No-not specified why"                  ~ "not_specified",
      TRUE                                                           ~ NA_character_
    ),
    listing_status = case_when(
      physician_at_location == "confirmed_yes"                      ~ "confirmed_valid",
      physician_at_location == "confirmed_no"                       ~ "confirmed_invalid",
      physician_active      == "confirmed_no"                       ~ "confirmed_invalid",
      phone_validity_flag   == "invalid_format"                     ~ "confirmed_invalid",
      is.na(office_answered) & is.na(taking_new_patients)          ~ "not_attempted",
      TRUE                                                          ~ "unresolved"
    ),
    listing_status = factor(listing_status,
                            levels = c("confirmed_valid", "confirmed_invalid",
                                       "unresolved", "not_attempted"))
  )

# ── Core counts ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
n_total             <- nrow(df)
n_nppes_aboto       <- sum(df$overlap_zone == "NPPES+ABOto",           na.rm = TRUE)
n_triple            <- sum(df$overlap_zone == "NPPES+ABOto+ENTHealth",  na.rm = TRUE)

# Listings that received at least one call attempt
n_not_attempted     <- sum(df$listing_status == "not_attempted",        na.rm = TRUE)
n_attempted         <- n_total - n_not_attempted     # primary denominator for validation rates

# Listings with a recorded office-answer status (used as denominator for reach rate)
n_office_status     <- sum(!is.na(df$office_answered))
n_reached           <- sum(df$office_answered == TRUE,                  na.rm = TRUE)
n_not_reached       <- sum(df$office_answered == FALSE,                 na.rm = TRUE)

# Physician presence
n_at_location       <- sum(df$physician_at_location == "confirmed_yes", na.rm = TRUE)
n_active_anywhere   <- sum(df$physician_active      == "confirmed_yes", na.rm = TRUE)
n_active_elsewhere  <- n_active_anywhere - n_at_location   # relocated but still practicing

# Listings with a definitive determination (confirmed valid or invalid)
n_confirmed_invalid <- sum(df$listing_status == "confirmed_invalid",    na.rm = TRUE)
n_unresolved        <- sum(df$listing_status == "unresolved",           na.rm = TRUE)
n_definitive        <- n_at_location + n_confirmed_invalid

# Scheduling
n_new_patients      <- sum(df$taking_new_patients == "Yes",             na.rm = TRUE)
n_scheduling_denom  <- sum(!is.na(df$taking_new_patients))

# Invalid reasons
n_retired           <- sum(df$invalid_reason == "retired_inactive",     na.rm = TRUE)
n_relocated_invalid <- sum(df$invalid_reason == "relocated",            na.rm = TRUE)

# Stratum-level counts — attempted (listing_status != "not_attempted") as denominator
n_aboto_attempted   <- sum(df$overlap_zone == "NPPES+ABOto" &
                           df$listing_status != "not_attempted",        na.rm = TRUE)
n_triple_attempted  <- sum(df$overlap_zone == "NPPES+ABOto+ENTHealth" &
                           df$listing_status != "not_attempted",        na.rm = TRUE)

n_valid_aboto       <- sum(df$overlap_zone == "NPPES+ABOto" &
                           df$listing_status == "confirmed_valid",      na.rm = TRUE)
n_valid_triple      <- sum(df$overlap_zone == "NPPES+ABOto+ENTHealth" &
                           df$listing_status == "confirmed_valid",      na.rm = TRUE)
n_invalid_aboto     <- sum(df$overlap_zone == "NPPES+ABOto" &
                           df$listing_status == "confirmed_invalid",    na.rm = TRUE)
n_invalid_triple    <- sum(df$overlap_zone == "NPPES+ABOto+ENTHealth" &
                           df$listing_status == "confirmed_invalid",    na.rm = TRUE)
n_unresolved_aboto  <- sum(df$overlap_zone == "NPPES+ABOto" &
                           df$listing_status == "unresolved",           na.rm = TRUE)
n_unresolved_triple <- sum(df$overlap_zone == "NPPES+ABOto+ENTHealth" &
                           df$listing_status == "unresolved",           na.rm = TRUE)

# Medicare Part B billing
n_billed            <- sum(df$billed_any_part_b == TRUE,                na.rm = TRUE)
n_billed_denom      <- sum(!is.na(df$billed_any_part_b))

# ── Helper functions ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
pct <- function(num, den) sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * num / den)

# Wilson score 95% CI for a single proportion
wilson_ci <- function(x, n, alpha = 0.05) {
  z <- qnorm(1 - alpha / 2)
  p <- x / n
  center <- (p + z^2 / (2 * n)) / (1 + z^2 / n)
  margin <- z * sqrt(p * (1 - p) / n + z^2 / (4 * n^2)) / (1 + z^2 / n)
  c(lower = center - margin, upper = center + margin)
}

fmt_ci <- function(ci) sprintf("%.1f%%-%.1f%%", 100 * ci["lower"], 100 * ci["upper"])

# Newcombe (1998) method 10 CI for the difference of two independent proportions
newcombe_diff <- function(x1, n1, x2, n2, alpha = 0.05) {
  p1 <- x1 / n1; p2 <- x2 / n2
  ci1 <- wilson_ci(x1, n1); ci2 <- wilson_ci(x2, n2)
  diff <- p2 - p1
  lo <- diff - sqrt((p1 - ci1["lower"])^2 + (ci2["upper"] - p2)^2)
  hi <- diff + sqrt((ci1["upper"] - p1)^2 + (p2 - ci2["lower"])^2)
  c(diff = diff, lower = lo, upper = hi)
}

# ── Wilson CIs for key estimates ──────────────────────────────────────────────
ci_valid_overall    <- wilson_ci(n_at_location, n_attempted)
ci_wf_overall       <- wilson_ci(n_active_anywhere, n_attempted)
ci_valid_definitive <- wilson_ci(n_at_location, n_definitive)
ci_valid_aboto      <- wilson_ci(n_valid_aboto,  n_aboto_attempted)
ci_valid_triple     <- wilson_ci(n_valid_triple, n_triple_attempted)
nc_diff             <- newcombe_diff(n_valid_aboto, n_aboto_attempted,
                                     n_valid_triple, n_triple_attempted)

# ── Sensitivity bounds ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Denominator = attempted (n_attempted = n_total - n_not_attempted)
pct_valid_worstcase <- pct(n_at_location,              n_attempted)  # unresolved → invalid
pct_valid_bestcase  <- pct(n_at_location + n_unresolved, n_attempted) # unresolved → valid
pct_valid_obs       <- pct(n_at_location, n_definitive)               # definitive only

# ── Geographic and temporal range ────────────────────────────────────────────
n_states   <- n_distinct(df$state)
call_start <- format(min(df$call_date, na.rm = TRUE), "%B %Y")
call_end   <- format(max(df$call_date, na.rm = TRUE), "%B %Y")
```

# Introduction

Accurate physician listings are necessary for patients to obtain specialty care and for health systems, insurers, and policymakers to estimate the available workforce. An outdated listing may direct a patient to the wrong telephone number or to a practice where the physician no longer works. At the population level, stale or misclassified records may also distort estimates of specialist availability and geographic access.

Previous studies have documented substantial inaccuracies in federal, commercial, and Medicaid physician directories.[@DesRoches2015; @Haeder2016; @Butala2024] However, most studies have evaluated insurer networks or nonsurgical specialties, and no national study has directly examined otolaryngology listings through telephone confirmation.

Otolaryngology is particularly suited to this question because several national sources are used to identify the specialty, yet each serves a different purpose. NPPES is an administrative registry, the American Board of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery (ABOto) identifies physicians with active board certification, and ENTHealth is a voluntary professional directory. We linked the three sources and conducted a stratified mystery-caller audit of otolaryngologists identified in NPPES. The primary outcome was confirmation that the physician currently worked at the contacted practice; the secondary outcome was continued active otolaryngology practice elsewhere. We hypothesized that corroborated listings would be more likely to represent current physicians.

\newpage

# Methods

*Data Sources and Record Linkage*

We conducted a national cross-sectional telephone audit of physicians identified in NPPES as otolaryngologists. The February 2026 NPPES dissemination file was searched for individual (Type 1) National Provider Identifiers with at least one taxonomy code beginning with 207Y. Records were linked by National Provider Identifier to the May 2026 ABOto active-certification roster and the May 2026 ENTHealth physician directory. Medicare Part B billing indicators for 2022 through 2023 were linked as a secondary measure of recent clinical activity. For physicians with multiple NPPES locations, the location designated as primary was selected; when no primary designation was available, the first listed location was used. The unit of analysis was one physician-location listing. Records with non-U.S., military, or diplomatic addresses were excluded from geographic analyses. The Old Dominion University Institutional Review Board determined that the study was non-human-subjects research (protocol 24-12-NH-0285).

*Sampling*

Registry linkage created four NPPES-based overlap groups: NPPES only, NPPES plus ABOto, NPPES plus ENTHealth, and a triple-match group present in all three sources (Table 1). The original mystery-caller cohort included `r comma(n_nppes_aboto)` listings from the NPPES-plus-ABOto group and `r comma(n_triple)` from the triple-match group. To characterize the NPPES-only group, a supplemental sample is underway. All eligible rural listings are being called, and approximately 325 nonrural listings were selected within AAO-HNS Board of Governors region and credential strata. The NPPES-plus-ENTHealth-only group was described in the source population but was not selected for telephone audit. The supplemental sample size was chosen to estimate a proportion near 50% with an approximate 5-percentage-point margin of error before accounting for stratification. Final population estimates will use inverse-probability weights based on the selection fraction within each sampling stratum.

*Telephone Audit*

Nine trained medical student callers placed calls under principal-investigator supervision. Callers completed standardized training in the scripts, call-attempt procedures, and REDCap data entry and were blinded to the study hypotheses.[@Harris2009REDCap] Before each call, the caller identified the physician's current practice website and used the telephone number displayed there rather than the NPPES telephone field, which could contain a personal mobile number. The audit therefore evaluated whether an NPPES-identified physician remained associated with a current practice; it did not directly test the accuracy of the NPPES telephone field. Eight subspecialty-specific scenarios were used, with a general otolaryngology scenario when fellowship training could not be confirmed. Listings without a definitive disposition received at least three attempts on different days and at different times. Voicemail without a returned call was not considered a definitive disposition.

*Outcomes*

The primary outcome was a practice-confirmed listing, defined as confirmation by practice staff that the named physician currently worked at the contacted practice and was actively seeing otolaryngology patients. The secondary outcome was workforce confirmation, defined as evidence that the physician remained in active otolaryngology practice, including at a different location. Each listing was classified as practice-confirmed, confirmed inaccurate, unresolved, or not attempted. Confirmed-inaccurate listings included physicians who had relocated or retired or were no longer practicing. Listings were classified as unresolved when the call protocol was completed without a definitive determination. Acceptance of new patients was analyzed separately as an access outcome and was not used to define listing validity.

*Statistical Analysis*

The current analysis is unweighted and is restricted to the original `r comma(n_total)`-listing cohort. Proportions are reported with Wilson 95% confidence intervals, and absolute differences between independent proportions are reported with Newcombe confidence intervals. Sensitivity analyses classified all unresolved listings first as practice-confirmed and then as confirmed inaccurate. After completion of the supplemental calls, final estimates will incorporate the stratified sampling design and inverse-probability weights using the `survey` package in R.[@Lumley2004survey] The prespecified adjusted model will include registry group, years since NPI enumeration, credential class, rurality, and geographic region. All tests will be two-sided, with P < .05 considered statistically significant. Analyses were performed in R version `r paste(R.version$major, R.version$minor, sep = ".")`.

\newpage

# Results

*Study Sample*

The linked registry universe contained `r comma(N_euler_total)` unique clinician records across seven overlap zones. Of these, `r comma(N_nppes_total)` were included in the four NPPES-based analytic groups: `r comma(N_nppes_only)` NPPES-only listings, `r comma(N_nppes_board)` NPPES-plus-ABOto listings, `r comma(N_nppes_ent)` NPPES-plus-ENTHealth listings, and `r comma(N_triple)` triple-match listings. The current audit included `r comma(n_total)` listings from the NPPES-plus-ABOto (n = `r comma(n_nppes_aboto)`) and triple-match (n = `r comma(n_triple)`) groups. Calls were placed from `r call_start` through `r call_end` across `r n_states` states. Medicare Part B billing information was available for `r comma(n_billed_denom)` listings, of which `r comma(n_billed)` (`r pct(n_billed, n_billed_denom)`) had recent billing activity.

*Practice Confirmation*

Of the `r comma(n_total)` sampled listings, `r comma(n_attempted)` received at least one call attempt and `r comma(n_not_attempted)` had no recorded disposition. Among `r comma(n_office_status)` attempted listings with a recorded office-answer status, callers reached a clinical practice for `r comma(n_reached)` (`r pct(n_reached, n_office_status)`). Overall, `r comma(n_at_location)` of `r comma(n_attempted)` attempted listings were practice-confirmed (`r pct(n_at_location, n_attempted)`; 95% CI, `r fmt_ci(ci_valid_overall)`). An additional `r comma(n_active_elsewhere)` physicians had relocated but remained in active practice, yielding workforce confirmation for `r comma(n_active_anywhere)` of `r comma(n_attempted)` attempted listings (`r pct(n_active_anywhere, n_attempted)`; 95% CI, `r fmt_ci(ci_wf_overall)`). Among the `r comma(n_definitive)` listings with a definitive valid or invalid determination, `r comma(n_at_location)` (`r pct(n_at_location, n_definitive)`; 95% CI, `r fmt_ci(ci_valid_definitive)`) were practice-confirmed. Of `r comma(n_scheduling_denom)` listings with a recorded scheduling disposition, `r comma(n_new_patients)` (`r pct(n_new_patients, n_scheduling_denom)`) were accepting new patients.

*Reasons for Unconfirmed Listings*

A total of `r comma(n_confirmed_invalid)` listings were confirmed inaccurate. The physician had retired or was no longer practicing in `r comma(n_retired)` cases (`r pct(n_retired, n_confirmed_invalid)`) and had relocated to another practice in `r comma(n_relocated_invalid)` (`r pct(n_relocated_invalid, n_confirmed_invalid)`). An additional `r comma(n_unresolved)` attempted listings remained unresolved after the call protocol. When all unresolved listings were classified as inaccurate, the practice-confirmation rate among attempted listings was `r pct_valid_worstcase`; when all unresolved listings were classified as confirmed, the rate was `r pct_valid_bestcase`.

*Comparison by Registry Group*

Among attempted listings, practice confirmation was `r pct(n_valid_aboto, n_aboto_attempted)` in the NPPES-plus-ABOto group (`r comma(n_valid_aboto)` of `r comma(n_aboto_attempted)`; 95% CI, `r fmt_ci(ci_valid_aboto)`) and `r pct(n_valid_triple, n_triple_attempted)` in the triple-match group (`r comma(n_valid_triple)` of `r comma(n_triple_attempted)`; 95% CI, `r fmt_ci(ci_valid_triple)`). The absolute difference was `r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * nc_diff["diff"])` percentage points (95% CI, `r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * nc_diff["lower"])`-`r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * nc_diff["upper"])` percentage points). Supplemental NPPES-only calls are ongoing; nationally weighted estimates and adjusted analyses will be reported after those calls are complete.

\newpage

# Discussion

In the completed portion of this national mystery-caller audit, practice confirmation was approximately `r sprintf("%.0f", 100 * nc_diff["diff"])` percentage points higher for listings found in NPPES, ABOto, and ENTHealth than for listings found in NPPES and ABOto alone. Three findings were most important. First, a substantial proportion of sampled listings remained unconfirmed because the physician had left practice, relocated, or could not be definitively verified. Second, agreement across independent data sources was strongly associated with confirmation at the contacted practice. Third, relocation and retirement represented distinct forms of listing inaccuracy with different implications for workforce measurement.

These findings extend prior provider-directory research to otolaryngology. Previous mystery-caller studies have often combined several barriers — including incorrect contact information, network participation, and acceptance of new patients — into a single measure of a phantom listing.[@Haeder2016; @Zhu2022; @Burman2022] Our primary outcome addressed a narrower question: whether an NPPES-identified physician could be confirmed in active otolaryngology practice at the contacted practice. This distinction matters because a physician who has relocated creates an inaccurate practice listing but may still contribute to the national workforce.

The association between registry corroboration and practice confirmation should not be interpreted as evidence that any single source is a gold standard. NPPES, ABOto, and ENTHealth were created for different purposes and contain different physician populations. Board certification and professional-directory participation may signal continued engagement with the specialty, but absence from either source does not establish that a physician is inactive. The supplemental NPPES-only audit is therefore essential to determine whether those records represent trainees, active physicians following other certification pathways, stale listings, or taxonomy misclassification.

This study has several limitations. Callers used telephone numbers from practice websites rather than the NPPES telephone field, so the results do not measure NPPES telephone-number accuracy. At the time of this analysis, `r comma(n_not_attempted)` sampled listings had no disposition and `r comma(n_unresolved)` attempted listings remained unresolved. Sensitivity analyses therefore provide bounds rather than a single definitive estimate. The cross-sectional design cannot determine when a listing became inaccurate or how long it had remained outdated. Callers were not blinded to registry group, although outcomes were recorded with standardized definitions and callers were blinded to the study hypotheses. For referral systems and workforce analyses, agreement across independent sources may offer a practical way to prioritize records for verification. However, corroboration should be used as a signal rather than as an automatic inclusion or exclusion rule. Final weighted analyses incorporating the NPPES-only sample will determine whether multi-source linkage meaningfully improves national estimates of the current otolaryngology workforce.

\newpage

# Conclusions

Among the two currently audited registry groups, listings corroborated by both ABOto and ENTHealth were substantially more likely to be confirmed at the contacted practice than listings corroborated by ABOto alone. Completion of the NPPES-only audit will determine whether registry corroboration can improve national otolaryngology workforce estimates and referral directories.

```{r table1, echo=FALSE}
t1 <- tibble::tibble(
  `Registry group`     = c("NPPES only",
                            "NPPES + ABOto",
                            "NPPES + ENTHealth",
                            "Triple match"),
  `Source population, N` = scales::comma(c(N_nppes_only, N_nppes_board,
                                            N_nppes_ent,  N_triple)),
  `Audited, n`           = c("379 planned",
                              scales::comma(n_nppes_aboto),
                              "0",
                              scales::comma(n_triple)),
  `Audit status`         = c("Supplemental calls ongoing",
                              "Current audit",
                              "Not sampled",
                              "Current audit"),
  `Sampling fraction`    = c("Pending final strata",
                              sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * n_nppes_aboto / N_nppes_board),
                              "0.0%",
                              sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * n_triple / N_triple))
)
kable(t1, align = c("l","r","r","l","r"),
      caption = "Table 1. Source population and telephone-audit sample by registry group.")
```

*Abbreviations: ABOto, American Board of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery; NPPES, National Plan and Provider Enumeration System.*

```{r table2, echo=FALSE}
t2 <- tibble::tibble(
  `Registry group`            = c("NPPES + ABOto",
                                   "Triple match",
                                   "Overall"),
  `Attempted, n`              = scales::comma(c(n_aboto_attempted,
                                                 n_triple_attempted,
                                                 n_attempted)),
  `Practice-confirmed, n (%)`  = c(
    sprintf("%d (%s)", n_valid_aboto,
            pct(n_valid_aboto,  n_aboto_attempted)),
    sprintf("%d (%s)", n_valid_triple,
            pct(n_valid_triple, n_triple_attempted)),
    sprintf("%d (%s)", n_at_location,
            pct(n_at_location,  n_attempted))
  ),
  `Confirmed inaccurate, n (%)` = c(
    sprintf("%d (%s)", n_invalid_aboto,
            pct(n_invalid_aboto,  n_aboto_attempted)),
    sprintf("%d (%s)", n_invalid_triple,
            pct(n_invalid_triple, n_triple_attempted)),
    sprintf("%d (%s)", n_confirmed_invalid,
            pct(n_confirmed_invalid, n_attempted))
  ),
  `Unresolved, n (%)`          = c(
    sprintf("%d (%s)", n_unresolved_aboto,
            pct(n_unresolved_aboto,  n_aboto_attempted)),
    sprintf("%d (%s)", n_unresolved_triple,
            pct(n_unresolved_triple, n_triple_attempted)),
    sprintf("%d (%s)", n_unresolved,
            pct(n_unresolved, n_attempted))
  )
)
kable(t2, align = c("l","r","r","r","r"),
      caption = "Table 2. Interim telephone-audit outcomes among attempted listings.")
```

*Percentages use attempted listings within each registry group as the denominator. An additional `r comma(n_not_attempted)` sampled listings had no recorded disposition.*

*Abbreviations: ABOto, American Board of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery; NPPES, National Plan and Provider Enumeration System.*

```{r table3, echo=FALSE}
t3 <- tibble::tibble(
  `Reason`                   = c("Retired or no longer practicing",
                                  "Relocated to another practice",
                                  "Total"),
  `n`                        = c(n_retired, n_relocated_invalid, n_confirmed_invalid),
  `% of confirmed inaccurate` = c(pct(n_retired,           n_confirmed_invalid),
                                   pct(n_relocated_invalid,  n_confirmed_invalid),
                                   "100.0%"),
  `Workforce interpretation` = c("Not workforce-confirmed",
                                  "Workforce-confirmed elsewhere",
                                  "")
)
kable(t3, align = c("l","r","r","l"),
      caption = "Table 3. Reasons for confirmed-inaccurate listings in the current sample.")
```

*Confirmed-inaccurate listings were mutually exclusive. Relocated physicians remained in the workforce but were not confirmed at the contacted practice.*

```{r supp-weights, echo=FALSE}
tibble::tibble(
  Stratum             = c("NPPES+ABOto", "NPPES+ABOto+ENTHealth", "NPPES-only (pending)"),
  `Population N`      = scales::comma(c(6748, 4573, 2756)),
  `Sampled n`         = c(scales::comma(498), scales::comma(462), "Pending"),
  `Sampling fraction` = c(sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * 498 / 6748),
                           sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * 462 / 4573),
                           "Pending"),
  `Weight`            = c(sprintf("%.2f", 6748 / 498),
                           sprintf("%.2f", 4573 / 462),
                           "Pending")
) |> kable(caption = "Supplementary Table S2. Sampling design and inverse-probability weights.")
```

*The rural NPPES-only group is sampled as a census; nonrural sampling weights will vary by region and credential stratum.*

```{r supp-table-s3, echo=FALSE}
ts3a <- df |>
  count(listing_status, name = "n") |>
  mutate(`%` = sprintf("%.1f", 100 * n / sum(n)),
         `Listing status` = as.character(listing_status)) |>
  select(`Listing status`, n, `%`)

ts3b <- df |>
  filter(listing_status == "confirmed_invalid") |>
  count(invalid_reason, sort = TRUE, name = "n") |>
  mutate(
    `% of invalid` = sprintf("%.1f", 100 * n / sum(n)),
    `Reason` = dplyr::recode(invalid_reason,
      retired_inactive          = "Retired or no longer practicing medicine",
      relocated                 = "Changed practices / relocated",
      wrong_disconnected_number = "Wrong or disconnected phone number",
      not_reached_valid_phone   = "Office not reached (valid phone number)",
      not_specified             = "Office answered; reason not specified",
      .default = invalid_reason)
  ) |>
  select(Reason, n, `% of invalid`)

kable(ts3a, caption = "Supplementary Table S3a. Listing-status distribution (unweighted; NPPES-only calls pending).")
kable(ts3b, caption = "Supplementary Table S3b. Reasons for confirmed-inaccurate listings.")
```

```{r supp-nppes-only, echo=FALSE}
nppes_only_file <- tail(sort(list.files(here("data", "processed"),
                                         pattern = "nppes_only_ent_ruca",
                                         full.names = TRUE)), 1)

if (length(nppes_only_file) > 0) {
  npo <- read_csv(nppes_only_file, show_col_types = FALSE)
  tibble::tibble(
    Characteristic    = c("Total (US addresses)",
                           "Rural (RUCA >=7)",
                           "Non-Rural (RUCA 1-6)",
                           "MD credential",
                           "DO credential",
                           "Missing credential",
                           "Enumeration <=5 years ago",
                           "Enumeration 6-10 years ago",
                           "Enumeration >10 years ago",
                           "NPI deactivated"),
    `n (%)`           = c(
      scales::comma(nrow(npo)),
      sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", sum(npo$ruca_binary == "Rural",  na.rm=TRUE),
              100*mean(npo$ruca_binary == "Rural",  na.rm=TRUE)),
      sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", sum(npo$ruca_binary == "Non-Rural", na.rm=TRUE),
              100*mean(npo$ruca_binary == "Non-Rural", na.rm=TRUE)),
      sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", sum(grepl("^M\\.?D\\.?$|^MD$", toupper(npo$credential), perl=TRUE), na.rm=TRUE),
              100*mean(grepl("^M\\.?D\\.?$|^MD$", toupper(npo$credential), perl=TRUE), na.rm=TRUE)),
      sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", sum(grepl("^D\\.?O\\.?$|^DO$", toupper(npo$credential), perl=TRUE), na.rm=TRUE),
              100*mean(grepl("^D\\.?O\\.?$|^DO$", toupper(npo$credential), perl=TRUE), na.rm=TRUE)),
      sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", sum(is.na(npo$credential) | npo$credential == "", na.rm=TRUE),
              100*mean(is.na(npo$credential) | npo$credential == "", na.rm=TRUE)),
      sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", sum(npo$years_since_enumeration <= 5, na.rm=TRUE),
              100*mean(npo$years_since_enumeration <= 5, na.rm=TRUE)),
      sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", sum(npo$years_since_enumeration %in% 6:10, na.rm=TRUE),
              100*mean(npo$years_since_enumeration %in% 6:10, na.rm=TRUE)),
      sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", sum(npo$years_since_enumeration > 10, na.rm=TRUE),
              100*mean(npo$years_since_enumeration > 10, na.rm=TRUE)),
      sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", sum(npo$is_deactivated == TRUE, na.rm=TRUE),
              100*mean(npo$is_deactivated == TRUE, na.rm=TRUE))
    )
  ) |> kable(caption = "Supplementary Table S4. Characteristics of NPPES-only ENT physicians (not in ABOto or ENTHealth).")
} else {
  cat("NPPES-only file not found.")
}
```
